messages:
Alex: FYI — follow-up from the RFC: proposal to introduce a small "q-edge" prefilter service in front of the console query layer to do RBAC prefiltering + tenant-scoped routing. Trying to capture tradeoffs quickly.
Priya: quick summary? sounds similar to earlier sidecar idea.
Alex: short: move minimal authz predicate evaluation and route-to-tenant mapping earlier (at q-edge) so the main query cluster sees already-filtered requests. Benefits: reduce fanout for heavy dashboards, fewer expensive auth calls per backend, and earlier caching.
Jordan: downside is duplication of RBAC logic and risk of divergence. Also adds another hop + possible cold-start. How do we ensure correctness?
Alex: agreed. plan is to keep q-edge extremely thin: only predicate evaluation using the authoritative authz service as the source of truth. q-edge would cache policy blobs for TTL=10s and validate tokens. Any mismatch should fall back to full evaluation in the query layer (fail-open -> fallback path).
Sam: what's the perf win we expect? numbers?
Alex: ballpark from sampling: dashboards with long fanout (200+ subqueries) see ~30-45% reduced p50/p95 when prefiltering drops half of tenants before backend. We'll run a small lab test to confirm.
Mia: cache invalidation is scary — if a policy revocation must be immediate. TTL=10s could be unacceptable for some enterprise customers. Need a plan for instant revocation.
Alex: good catch. plan: push critical revocations (user suspends, high-risk changes) through an invalidate pub/sub channel. q-edge subscribes to topic and evicts relevant entries. Non-critical changes still TTL-based.
Jordan: how about consistency during rollout? If some q-edge nodes have old blobs and others new, queries might get inconsistent results.
Priya: we can namespace requests with an "auth-version" header. Query layer always treats results as authoritative only if auth-version matches its own cached policy version. Otherwise it triggers full re-check. That maintains safety but reduces some perf for mismatched requests.
Sam: can we re-use existing gateway infra? worried about more operational surface area.
Alex: yes, we should reuse gateway LB and auto-scale groups. q-edge will be a small service (go) with fewer memory requirements. We only want one additional hop, not another full fleet.
Mia: what about metrics and tracing? If we short-circuit backends we need clear telemetry to show where filters hit.
Alex: agreed — q-edge will emit tags: prefilter.hits, prefilter.misses, fallback.full-check. Add a telemetry dashboard and a per-tenant breakdown.
Jordan: rollout plan?
Alex: propose phased rollout: 1) lab load-tests (compare against baseline) 2) internal canary on low-risk tenants behind feature flag (2 weeks) 3) broader canary on 5% production traffic with strict SLO guards 4) full opt-in for customers; some enterprise tenants can stay on legacy path until they opt in.
Priya: who owns the feature flag / opt-in? Product + customer success for enterprise toggles. Eng-platform owns the infra flagging.
Sam: what about security review? moving auth decisions earlier might require extra review from security/compliance.
Alex: will request formal security sign-off and run a threat model doc. Also add pen-test of q-edge.
Mia: small nit: please add a kill-switch that flips q-edge to passthrough to avoid impacting customers if something goes wrong.
Alex: yes — global kill-switch + per-tenant override.
deploy-bot: build/ci: q-edge main -> build succeeded (sha: a1b2c3).
Alex: Action items: (1) Jordan + Alex -> prototype lab tests this week. (2) Priya -> draft opt-in flag and enterprise opt-out flow. (3) Mia -> draft invalidation pub/sub pattern + security review checklist. (4) Sam -> perf dashboard mockups. I'll post a short RFC update after lab runs.
Priya: SGTM.
Jordan: I'll pair with Alex on the lab harness tomorrow.
Mia: adding security review meeting to calendar.
Sam: will sketch a dashboard by EOD.
Alex: thanks — will update thread with numbers once we have load tests.
